vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of an End of File (EOF) check when reading the 'extent' field in the Photoshop profile section of a PostScript file.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: A crafted PostScript file that claims a large 'extent' field in the header but does not provide sufficient backing data is processed.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The function attempts to read more data than is actually present in the file, leading to repeated calls to ProfileInteger(image, hex_digits) without checking if the end of the file has been reached. This causes the CPU to be consumed indefinitely.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to add an EOF check before attempting to read the data into the profile. Specifically, the function should check if the 'length' (the claimed size of the data) is greater than the actual size of the file (GetBlobSize(image)). If the 'length' exceeds the file size, the function should throw a CorruptImageError exception with the message 'InsufficientImageDataInFile'. This stops further processing and prevents the CPU from being consumed indefinitely.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to add end-of-file (EOF) checks during file reading operations. This ensures that the function terminates gracefully when it encounters the end of the file, preventing infinite loops and excessive CPU usage. In this case, the solution involves adding checks to see if ReadBlobByte(image) returns EOF, and breaking out of the loop if EOF is encountered. Additionally, explicit EOF checks should be added after the main reading loop and in nested loops where data is being read from specific sections of the DPX file.
